summary.text: Mai Vang is a Sacramento City Council member for District 8 and the daughter of Hmong refugees from Laos. A former school board member, city council staffer and nonprofit director, she was first elected to the council in 2020 and finished first in the June 2026 top-two primary. She is challenging fellow Democrat Doris Matsui.

paragraphs.text: According to the City of Sacramento, Vang is the daughter of Hmong refugees from Laos, a Sacramento native, and the eldest of 16 children.
Holds bachelor's degrees in biology and sociology from the University of San Francisco and master's degrees in public health and Asian American studies from UCLA.
Worked as a community organizer on health and educational outcomes for children and families in south Sacramento, and co-founded Hmong Innovating Politics (HIP), a civic engagement organization.

Served as Community Affairs Director for Sacramento Councilmember Larry Carr at City Hall from 2014 to 2018, and as executive director of the Buck Scholars Association, which provides mentorship and scholarships to high school students.
Served on the Sacramento City Unified School District board (Area 5) from 2016 to 2020.
Elected in November 2020 to the Sacramento City Council representing District 8 (South Sacramento); her term runs through 2028.

Her council office's biography lists first-term work including the Measure L Sacramento Children's Fund ballot initiative, a Food Justice Task Force, and a city purchase of 102 acres in South Sacramento for future development; the Sacramento Bee named her a top AAPI Change Maker in 2022.
Teaches in the Department of Ethnic Studies at California State University, Sacramento, and has taught Asian American Studies at UC Davis; lives in the Meadowview neighborhood of South Sacramento.
Has not completed Ballotpedia's 2026 Candidate Connection survey.
